messages:
maria_support: Customer (acme) reporting truncated streaming responses. The client gets a bunch of data frames, then the connection goes quiet — final JSON object never closed and finish_reason is absent. They say it reliably happens while their client rotates tokens (refresh request) and are on HTTP/2 behind a corporate proxy.

maria_support: They captured a sample where the last visible SSE lines were ok but no terminal event. Paste of the tail:
```
data: {"id":"req-9f5","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Thanks for using our"}}]}
data: {"id":"req-9f5","choices":[{"delta":{"content":" service.\n"}}]}
# connection silent, no final chunk with finish_reason/stop
```

sam_engineer: thanks — can you get raw http/2 frames or the proxy logs? does client see GOAWAY or RST_STREAM? any HTTP status on the last request? :thinking_face:

maria_support: customer attached tcpdump excerpt — I pasted the relevant frame summary they gave us:
```
[14:22:10.123] <- RST_STREAM (stream_id=5, error_code=NO_ERROR)
[14:22:10.124] client sends new AUTH refresh
[14:22:10.125] stream 5 never gets final DATA/END_STREAM
```

jordan_oncall: that RST_STREAM with NO_ERROR plus token refresh timing smells like a proxy or client doing connection reset at token swap. Could be their side, but we should rule out transient behavior in our gateway when upstream auth rotation occurs.

kevin_prod: I checked our ingress logs around that time for req-9f5: backend returned 200 chunks streaming, no 5xx. No explicit GOAWAY from our side. But I do see a short TCP FIN to the upstream at 14:22:09. Might be their proxy closing idle streams during auth flow.

sam_engineer: can reproduce locally with a simple script if I force a http2 RST from a mutating proxy. Repro steps I used:
```
# start a simple http2 proxy that resets streams on header mutation
# 1) start service: node stream-server.js
# 2) start proxy that issues RST_STREAM when it sees Authorization change
# 3) curl -v -N --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://<proxy>/v1/streams -d '@req.json'
# then rotate token client-side and send new HEADERS on same connection
```
Observed result: SSE/streaming body stopped mid-object, client JSON parse error (unexpected EOF). finish_reason missing because final sentinel never sent.

maria_support: customer workaround: switched to HTTP/1.1 streaming and the issue went away. They need a more permanent fix — either we harden how gateway/keepalive behaves on http/2 auth rotation or recommend token rotation strategy that opens a fresh connection instead of mutating headers in-place.

jordan_oncall: action items:
- sam_engineer to add instrumentation to detect RST_STREAM/GOAWAY during active streaming and log paired request ids (sam)
- kevin_prod to look at upstream keepalive / connection teardown behavior and whether we close streams on auth-change (kevin)
- maria_support to confirm customer can accept http/1.1 workaround for now and collect full pcap (maria)

infra-bot: INC-2026-045 created and linked to this thread.

sam_engineer: quick patch idea: if we observe header mutation that triggers proxy-reset, try to emit a synthetic final event with finish_reason:\"internal_connection_reset\" before closing on our side. Will prototype.

maria_support: customer ok with temporary workaround; they've uploaded pcap to ticket. Marking as escalated to eng-runtime.

kevin_prod: noted — tagging eng-runtime and routing to eng-infra for gateway review.

maria_support: thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and follow up once we get a repro-tested mitigation. :thumbsup:
